High-level asks:

- Quantization: which model families and precisions do you recommend for 8-bit/4-bit flows that still meet our quality bar? Any known tradeoffs for long-context dialogs (>4k tokens).
- Batching & caching: expected latency/throughput impact and a concrete example of token savings if we enable prefix KV caching for session reuse.
- Any quick trial credits or sandbox to validate throughput/quality with our prompt set?

We want something concise we can put in front of our CFO and infra lead. If you prefer a quick 20-minute call today, I can make time.

Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I attached a short provisional SOW that maps the commercial examples to service levels. Happy to hop on a quick sync if you prefer.

1) Commercial example (ballpark):
- Trial: $10k in Optimize credits (apply to token units & Tooling advisor reports) for 30 days to validate with your prompt set.
- Entry reserved (monthly): $6k/mo commit --> equates to ~15% list discount + 500k toolkit credits/month.
- Mid commit: $18k/mo --> ~20% list discount + 2M credits/month + 24/7 support.
- Enterprise (annual): custom pricing, deeper discounts with multi-region private deployment.

2) Quantization guidance (short):
- Recommend starting with 8-bit (GPT-style models and Llama2 derivatives) for most flows; quality drop is typically <2–3% on classification/QA tasks.
- 4-bit (QLoRA / FP4) can be OK for high-volume, low-sensitivity generations but expect larger variance on long coherent completions.
- For >4k contexts, we suggest offloading long-term memory to a document store + prefix caching for immediate context to keep KV sizes manageable.

3) Batching & caching example:
- If you enable continuous batching + prefix KV caching for sessions with 60% repeated prefixes, token compute can drop ~30–45% depending on average turn length.
- Latency: batching adds ~5–20ms P50 per request in our tests; P95 depends on traffic shaping and can be tuned.

4) Trial credits: we can offer the $10k credit above and a 2-week dedicated se session with Marcus to run your prompts.

Next steps: attached SOW (novum_SOW_v1.pdf). Marcus will follow up on the quantization benchmarks. If that looks good we can draft a 60-day pilot + signed MSA.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Elena — looping in technical notes and a tiny benchmark sample (attached). A few concrete items you can use for modeling: 

- Quantization: in our internal tests with Llama2-13B derivatives:
  * 8-bit (int8): token throughput improves ~1.8x vs FP16 with negligible BLEU/ROUGE changes on typical dialog prompts.
  * 4-bit (nf4/aq): throughput improves ~2.6x but you should validate on multi-turn coherence — we saw hallucination risk uptick on loosely constrained prompts.

- Long context (>4k): keep hot KV for the last ~1k tokens in-memory; compress older turns into embeddings and fetch as needed. That pattern preserves persona and reduces end-to-end compute ~20–35%.

- Batching: continuous batching helps at steady qps; if your peak traffic is spiky, consider our burst pools to keep P95 latency from degrading.

Example savings scenario (conservative):
- Baseline: 1.0M tokens/day
- With 8-bit + prefix caching (60% repeated): ~400k tokens saved/month (~40% reduction)
- With 4-bit + caching: ~600k tokens saved (~60% reduction) but expect a QA/LLM-quality delta to measure.

I attached quant_benchmarks.csv with per-model numbers (throughput, P50/P95, quality delta). Happy to run that file against Novum prompts in the sandbox.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
